newsitem.title: UK: London, Tokyo stocks edge higher.
newsitem.headline: London, Tokyo stocks edge higher.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Monday.

LONDON - The stock market ended the third quarter on a quiet but positive note, with a rout among utilities offset by selective buying of other blue chips. The FTSE 100 share index reversed modest early losses to end the day at 3,953.7 points, up 7.3 points. That brought the gain in the last three months to 242.7 points, almost the entire year's rise for the blue-chip indicator.

FRANKFURT - German shares ended bourse trade lower amid evidence of profit-taking after last week's highs, but off earlier lows and keeping an eye out for U.S. data due in the afternoon. The 30-share blue chip DAX index ended down 7.19 points at 2,651.85 points. In post-bourse trade the index fell 4.37 to 2,655.49.

PARIS - French shares closed sharply higher as September futures expired in a bullish mood helped by an early rise in the Dow Jones index. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 25.76 points at 2,132.81.

ZURICH - Swiss shares shook off early weariness to close above important resistance levels of 3,700 and 3,710 points in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI). The all-share SPI was up 20.88 points to 2,393.95.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed modestly higher, with trading remaining quiet on the last day of the first half year of the financial year. Brokers said the market's attention was shifting to how the key stock index would move from Oct. 1. The key 225-share Nikkei average finished up 9.38 points at 21,556.40.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks soared ahead trade with the Hang Seng index jumping to new 1996 highs on an improved outlook for interest rates and upward revisions in corporate earnings forecasts. The Hang Seng Index put on 143.04 points to close at 11,902.43.

SYDNEY - Australian shares closed firmer after the market scrambled off its lows in the afternoon ahead of the September share index futures expiry. The All Ordinaries index gained 7.4 points to 2,290.40. Brokers said a spurt of activity in the leaders in the afternoon saw the bourse head to higher ground.

JOHANNESBURG - South African gold shares were battered by a sickly gold price which also dampened sentiment in industrial shares. The overall index fell 55.2 points to 6,878.0 points, the industrial index shed 48.6 points to 8,130.6 points and the gold index dropped 43.3 points, or 2.55 percent, to 1,653.7 points.
